title: Tools and permissions
bridge: allowedTools is like the allow-list in a browser CSP: a fixed list of what may run without asking. Except: it only auto-approves. The model still has every built-in tool until you remove it with disallowedTools or shrink the base set with tools.
intro: Nobody sits at a prompt when Nova runs, so every tool call must be decided in advance. This lesson gives a session its tools back and shows the four options that decide what runs: tools, allowedTools, disallowedTools and permissionMode. It also covers which settings files load and how the system prompt is set.

picture.caption: The model asks for a tool. A permission check answers from your lists, then from the mode. Refusals are recorded in the result.

steps.text: asks to call Write with a file path
is Write in disallowedTools? then the model never saw it
is Write in allowedTools? then it runs now
neither: what does the mode say?
dontAsk: refused, and the model is told why
the refusal is recorded on the result message

p: tools sets the base set of built-in tools. The preset gives Claude Code's full set; an array names a few; [] means none. allowedTools is the list of tools that run without asking. disallowedTools removes tools from the model's view completely.
These are different questions. A tool can exist and still need approval. A tool in allowedTools is approved, but if it is not in the base set it does not exist. Keep the three apart in your head.
sections.because: We spell out each list because mixing them up is the most common reason a headless session does nothing.

notes.text: cwd is the folder the tools work in. Read and Glob are relative to it.
Built-in tool names are exact: Read, Glob, Grep, Edit, Write, Bash, TodoWrite, Workflow.
A bare name removes the tool. A scoped rule like 'Bash(rm *)' keeps Bash and denies matching calls.
Write is not in any list. Under dontAsk the model may try it, and it is refused.

sections.h: permissionMode: pick dontAsk for headless runs
p: A permission mode says what happens to a tool call that no list decided. The modes are default (ask a person), acceptEdits (file edits pass) and plan (no tool runs). Then bypassPermissions (everything passes), auto (a model classifier decides) and dontAsk.
dontAsk means: never ask, deny anything not pre-approved. That is the mode for every session in the platform. There is no person to ask, and we want refusals to be explicit and recorded.

Set it every time. If you leave it out, the session starts in whatever mode the loaded settings or the binary pick. In a VM with no API key, Claude Code cannot fetch feature flags, so the ticket says: set the mode yourself.

callout.text: bypassPermissions is not 'faster dontAsk'. It passes everything, including dangerous commands. The platform never uses it.

p: A refused call does not crash the session. The model is told the call was denied and goes on. At the end, result.permission_denials lists every denial with tool_name and tool_input. That is the authoritative record.
The lab asks the model to list files and then create one. Read and Glob pass. The Write call is refused, and the model reports that it could not create the file.
sections.because: We print permission_denials because a quiet refusal is a bug you only find when a PR is missing a file.

notes.text: One prompt with an allowed action and a forbidden one, so you see both paths in one run.
permission_denials is on every result. Each entry has tool_name, tool_use_id and tool_input.
result is the model's final text. Here it should say the file was not created.

sections.see:
result success
denied [ 'Write' ]
said I listed the folder (package.json, src, node_modules) but could not create hello.txt: the Write tool was denied.
sections.ifInstead: If instead denied prints [] and hello.txt exists, permissionMode was not set to dontAsk. Or a settings file with an allow rule loaded. Check settingSources: [].

p: Claude Code reads settings from files: user (~/.claude/settings.json), project (.claude/settings.json in cwd) and local (.claude/settings.local.json). settingSources picks which of these load. Omit it and all three load, like the CLI. Pass [] and none load.
Settings files carry permission rules, hooks and more. CLAUDE.md files only load when 'project' is included. Managed settings, the policy tier an admin controls, load regardless of this option.

The harness uses ['project'] in the fcp checkout. So fcp's AGENTS.md, .claude/ hooks and skills apply to Nova as they apply to a person. Judges and the QA agent use [] so nothing from the repo leaks into their context.

callout.text: Precedence: local over project over user; your options object overrides files; managed settings override your options.

sections.h: systemPrompt: the preset plus our guide
p: The system prompt is the standing instruction the model reads before your prompt. There are three shapes.
A plain string means you write everything. The preset is Claude Code's own prompt. The preset with append is Claude Code's prompt plus your text.
Nova uses the preset with append, so it keeps Claude Code's tool knowledge and adds our guide. A judge uses a plain string, because it should know nothing about editing code.
sections.because: We append to the preset instead of replacing it. The preset is what makes the model good at using the built-in tools.

notes.text: preset 'claude_code' is the only preset. append is a string added at the end.
A string replaces the preset completely. The model then has no tool guidance, which is right for a judge.
Keep append stable across turns: a changing system prompt breaks the prompt cache (p8-8).

p: Here is the real list from session.ts. Nova gets the editing tools, TodoWrite, the Workflow tool for p8-7, and our three MCP tools from p8-3. WebFetch and WebSearch are removed, because the proxy blocks the web anyway and we want to say so up front.

The reviewer in G4-18 gets only Read, Grep and Glob. No Bash: git diff --no-index or --output= would let it read or write outside the repo. The QA agent in G4-24 gets Read and the browser server, and a path-scoped deny on /work/fcp.
sections.because: We name every tool Nova may use because dontAsk refuses everything else, and a missing name shows up as a silent failure.

code.text:
settingSources: ["project"], // fcp's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and .claude/; managed settings load anyway
allowedTools: ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Edit", "Write", "Bash", "TodoWrite",
  "Workflow", "mcp__nova__ask_human", "mcp__nova__post_progress", "mcp__nova__kb_search"], // Workflow: G4-09, G4-19
disallowedTools: ["WebFetch", "WebSearch"], // the proxy blocks the web anyway; say so up front
permissionMode: "dontAsk", // nobody sits at a prompt: anything not allowed is refused

notes.text: 'project' loads fcp's repo rules. The managed tier (settings/managed-settings.d) loads on its own.
mcp__nova__ask_human is the name of our own tool: mcp__<server>__<tool>. Lesson p8-3 builds it.
Removed, not refused: the model does not see these tools at all.
Set explicitly. With no API key the binary cannot fetch defaults, so never rely on them.

quiz.q: A tool is in allowedTools but the model never calls it, and init's tools list does not show it. Why?

options.text: allowedTools only approves; the tool is missing from the base set (tools) or removed by disallowedTools
options.why: Approval and existence are separate questions; a tool that is not in the base set does not exist.

options.text: permissionMode must be bypassPermissions for allowedTools to work
options.why: allowedTools works in every mode; bypassPermissions would pass everything else too.

options.text: The model needs the tool in the system prompt
options.why: Tools are given through options, not the prompt; the preset explains how to use them.

quiz.q: Which permissionMode does every platform session use, and why?

options.text: default, so a person can approve risky calls
options.why: There is no person at a prompt in a VM; the session would hang or deny by default.

options.text: bypassPermissions, because the VM is isolated
options.why: It passes everything, including commands the walls forbid; the platform never uses it.

options.text: dontAsk, so unlisted tools are refused and the refusal is recorded
options.why: No prompts, explicit deny, and every denial lands in result.permission_denials.
The managed policy tier loads regardless of settingSources.

options.text: Loads no user, project or local settings file, and no CLAUDE.md
options.why: That is SDK isolation mode; judges use it so nothing from the repo leaks in.

options.text: Loads the defaults the CLI would load
options.why: Omitting the option loads all sources; [] loads none.

words.plain: A function the model can call by name, such as Read, Bash or Write; the SDK runs it and returns the output.
The base set of built-in tools a session has: the preset, a list of names, or [] for none.
Tools that run without asking anyone.
Tools removed from the model's view, or scoped rules that deny matching calls.
What happens to a tool call no list decided; dontAsk means refuse it and record it.
Which settings files load: user, project, local; [] loads none; 'project' is needed for CLAUDE.md.
The standing instruction before your prompt: a string, the claude_code preset, or the preset plus append.

tickets.why: session.ts is this lesson's options object: allowedTools, disallowedTools, dontAsk, settingSources ['project'] and the preset prompt.
The reviewer gets Read, Grep and Glob only; this lesson explains why Bash is removed.
The QA agent's options use settingSources [], a plain system prompt and a path-scoped deny.
The co-sign session has tools: [] and settingSources: []; now you know what both mean.

remember: tools says what exists, allowedTools what runs, disallowedTools what is gone; dontAsk refuses the rest and records it.
